title: perf(canary): add adaptive auto-detection and rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Priya Desai
release_notes: Added adaptive canary detector and rollout guards to automatically detect latency/throughput regressions and prevent unsafe rollouts. No behavioral API changes. Config flags allow tuning thresholds and hysteresis.
description:
Summary: Add an adaptive auto-detection pipeline for the performance canary system and a compact set of rollout guards to prevent automated rollouts on spurious regressions. Motivation: We saw intermittent high-p99 regressions during model rollouts that were noisy and caused manual rollbacks. This change reduces operator toil by (1) making detection traffic-aware and KV-cache-aware, (2) introducing hysteresis and cooldown windows, and (3) wiring deterministic rollback/hold semantics into the rollout controller.

Approach: Implemented a new detector that computes an anomaly score using a rolling-window baseline per-route and per-model-variant, normalizing by sample variance and traffic volume. The detector adapts thresholds based on historical percentile distributions (p50/p95) and requires a minimum sample count before firing. We added hysteresis (hold-until-stable) and a cooldown window to avoid flip-flopping decisions. The rollout guard integrates multiple signals (latency p95/p99, throughput drops, error-rate, GPU utilization, KV cache hit-rate) and applies weighted heuristics before blocking or rolling back a canary.

Key behavioral notes: No changes to public APIs. Default thresholds are conservative and can be tuned via canary-config. The detector respects dedicated vs hosted tiers (different min_samples and sensitivity). Rollout outcome: when a canary is blocked, the controller either holds traffic at the current percentage or rolls back to the last known good variant depending on severity.

Tests & CI: Unit tests for detector math + hysteresis, integration test that injects latency regressions and asserts guard behavior, and an end-to-end perf-canary job that runs on our perf-lab. Initial run surfaced a flaky assertion fixed by increasing a test timeout and improving fake metrics timing. All CI checks passed on rerun.

Rollout plan: Feature-flag gated, staged rollout: start with internal orgs, then canary for low-traffic customers, then global. Safety: automatic blocking is conservative; operators can override and force a rollout if needed.

Commits (high-level): - add adaptive detector + unit tests - integrate detector into canary controller - add rollout guard policy engine + tests - add prometheus rules and dashboard panels - docs: perf-canary guide + tuning notes - infra: helm chart config for canary thresholds

Files changed (high level): see files_changed list for paths.

Review summary & merge: Reviewed by Ethan, Marta, Samir. Addressed feedback to include KV-cache hit-rate and reduce false positives by requiring min_samples. CI passed after one fix. Squash-merged into main by Marta Ruiz.

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Can we ensure the detector is KV-cache-aware? Past regressions were often cache-thrashing artifacts.
Priya Desai: Added KV-cache attribution and included cache-hit-rate in the weighted signals. See internal/metrics/attribution.go change.
Marta Ruiz: We should be conservative with automatic rollback for high-traffic customers. Can you add a sensitivity profile for dedicated tiers?
Priya Desai: Added sensitivity profiles (default/low/enterprise) and feature-flag gating in config.go. Default is conservative for dedicated/enterprise tiers.
Samir Patel: Integration test looks flaky locally - the timing assumptions in the fake metrics provider are tight. Recommend increasing timeouts or using deterministic clock.
Priya Desai: Switched e2e fixture to deterministic fake clock and increased timeouts in the test. Fixed the flake.
Ethan Cole: CI reported a failing unit test initially (race in detector). Looks resolved in latest commit - verified the race was addressed by locking the baseline cache.
Marta Ruiz: Approving after tests pass. Suggest follow-up to expose per-route tuning in the console UI.
ci_log_summary: Initial CI: unit tests failed (detector race) and one integration test flake. Fixes pushed (locking baseline cache + deterministic fixture). Rerun: all checks passed. Perf pipeline: perf-canary job ran on perf-lab and reported expected anomaly detection in synthetic/regression scenarios.
merge_commit_message: feat(canary): adaptive auto-detect + rollout guards\n\nAdaptive detector, rollout guard policy engine, hysteresis and helm config. See perf-canary.md for tuning.
notes_for_operators: Feature gated: canary.auto_detect.enabled=false by default for existing clusters. To enable: update helm values charts.redwood.canary.autoDetect.enabled=true and tune sensitivity profiles. Recommended to start with 'default' profile for 48h on internal traffic before widening.
